name: Kurumba, Kannada
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2006. Change Request 2006-007 (submitted by Barb Waugh, SIL): rename [kfi] Kurumba -> Kannada Kurumba. Adopted 2007-07-18.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; a name change only ('To distinguish this from the newly proposed Kurumba language [tentatively pkr]'); the only source cited is personal communication from a language worker.

sources.citation: Hiremath, R. C. 1988. [Survey of Kannada dialect studies], International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics 17(1), p. 52
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; confirms Varma 1978 'gives a brief description of the Kannada dialect as spoken in Tamilnadu. It duly contains phonological and Morphological sections and a list of vocabulary.'

sources.citation: Srinivasa Varma, G. 1978. Kurumba Kannada (Pudukkottai Kurumba Dialect). Annamalainagar: Annamalai University, Department of Linguistics, Publication No. 59. vii+92 pp. (Glottolog ref 315889, filed under Kannada [kan]; it is the source Glottolog's kann1253 bookkeeping note cites for kfi being a Kannada dialect)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Chapter 1 Phonology (pp. 1-25) lists 24 segmental + 2 suprasegmental phonemes; §1.4 p. 9: 'There are two supra-segmental phonemes in this dialect. One is internal open juncture marked by / - / symbol and the other is length which occurs with vowels as simultaneous feature marked by /:/.' Syllable types §1.8 pp. 21-23, phonological changes §1.9 pp. 23-25. No token of stress/accent/prominence/intonation/pitch anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent over full text).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page kann1253 'Bookkeeping: Kurumba, Kannada' (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), comment on ISO kfi
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; establishes identity: kfi 'is meant to subsume Kurumba groups who speak varieties close to Kannada' (already coded xua, xuj, xub, pkr) but 'the large number of speakers indicated, as well as the name, is consistent with the entry referring to the large community of shepherds in Tamil Nadu (Aiyappan 1948: 125-128).. their language is a dialect of Kannada and thus covered in the Kannada [kan] entry (G. Srinivasa Varma 1978)'.

sources.citation: Srinivasa Varma, G. 1978. Kurumba Dialect of Kannada. In: Prof. R. C. Hiremath Felicitation Volume. Dharwar.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Companion article by the same author on the same Pudukkottai dialect (listed in the monograph's bibliography, p. 92); unlikely to add a stress statement given the monograph has none, but it is the only other primary treatment.

sources.citation: Upadhyaya, U. P. 1968. The Kurumba Language. Linguistic Survey Bulletin (Deccan College, Poona) 1: 7-12.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Cited in Varma 1978's bibliography (p. 92) as the only other dedicated description of a 'Kurumba' Kannada variety; short LSB sketches of this series sometimes carry a one-line accent note.

sources.citation: Blair, Frank et al. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Kurumba Dialects. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-015. Dallas: SIL International.

sources.note: Only modern work explicitly on the kfi communities; would settle which Tamil Nadu 'Kannada Kurumba' varieties the ISO code covers (identity), though it is a wordlist/intelligibility survey and probably says nothing on stress.
